verdict.probe_answer: Both arms' new tests reference symbols (RetryToml, WorkflowNodeToml.retry, RetryPolicy) that don't exist pre-change, so all would fail to compile against pre-change code — expected for TDD on new fields. Arm A: 4 tests. `workflow_node_retry_parses` (weakest — boilerplate deser check mirroring the task's literal example). `workflow_node_retry_maps_into_graph` (strongest, PR-FIX-9-mandated) drives the real `RegistryConfig::parse`+`load_workflows` path and asserts `WorkflowGraph.nodes[0].retry` equals the exact `RetryPolicy`, proving the mapping isn't dead code. Two extra tests add real edge coverage: `..._absent_defaults_to_none_end_to_end` proves the `None` arm of the `.map()` also survives into the graph (a distinct path from the Some case), and `..._missing_max_attempts_fails_to_parse` proves `max_attempts` has no serde default — a genuine requiredness assertion, not tautological. Arm B: 2 tests — a functionally identical `_parses` (weakest, though it adds a `backoff_cap_ms==None` check Arm A omits) and an identical `_maps_into_graph` (strongest, same PR-FIX-9 assertion as Arm A). Arm B never exercises the retry-absent or missing-required-field paths. Both arms' PR-FIX-9 tests assert real behavior via concrete struct equality against actual graph output, not trivial passes. Net: Arm A has broader edge/negative coverage; Arm B is narrower but not weaker on the mandated test itself.
verdict.rationale: Both arms implement identical RetryToml + WorkflowNodeToml.retry + graph-mapping code in config.rs, and both include the PR-FIX-9-mandated `workflow_node_retry_maps_into_graph` test verifying the real load_workflows path. Arm A stays entirely within config.rs as the task specifies and adds two extra in-scope edge tests (negative required-field test, absent->None end-to-end). Arm B additionally edits crates/bridge-workflow/src/graph.rs, changing `checked_mul().unwrap_or(MAX)` to `saturating_mul` in `backoff_for` — a behaviorally-equivalent simplification, but out of scope for a task explicitly scoped to config.rs 'no more'; that touches prior-task (T2) code this task shouldn't modify. That scope violation (SMELL, not a correctness bug) plus Arm A's stronger, broader test coverage make Arm A materially better overall.
